topic.subject: chemistry
topic.title: Chemical analysis, separation and interpreting evidence
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26 Chemistry map: Analysis; KS3 national curriculum supplies method detail
topic.overview: Chemical analysis combines careful observations with suitable separation or comparison methods. A conclusion should be no stronger than the evidence allows.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Qualitative data describe qualities such as colour or precipitate; quantitative data are numerical measurements.
Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid.
Evaporation or crystallisation recovers a dissolved solid; simple distillation recovers a solvent.
Chromatography separates dissolved substances because they travel differently with a solvent.
A pure substance has a sharp characteristic melting/boiling point; mixtures commonly melt or boil over a range.
Identify an unknown by comparing more than one reliable property or test with reference evidence.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: numerical evidence with a quantity and usually a unit
separating an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter
forming solid crystals from a solution
evaporating and condensing to collect a liquid
separating dissolved substances by different movement through a medium
one substance with characteristic fixed physical properties
two or more substances not chemically bonded

workedExamples.prompt: Choose a method to obtain sand from salt water containing sand.
workedExamples.answer: Filter first to collect sand; the salt remains dissolved in the filtrate.

workedExamples.prompt: A sample melts from 78-84 C while a pure reference melts at 80 C. Interpret.
workedExamples.answer: The broad range suggests the sample is impure or a mixture.

practicals.title: Separate a sand-salt mixture
practicals.aim: Recover sand and salt from a mixture.
practicals.variables: Track recovered masses; keep initial sample and water volume recorded.
practicals.method: Add water to dissolve salt, filter to collect and dry sand, then evaporate some water and crystallise the salt.
practicals.expectedResult: Sand remains as residue; salt crystals form from the filtrate.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection; heat gently and stop before heating to dryness; use tongs for hot apparatus.
practicals.evaluation: Dry products before weighing, minimise transfers, rinse residue and compare recovered total with starting mass.

commonMistakes: Using filtration to remove dissolved salt.
Evaporating to dryness when crystals are required.
Treating one colour observation as proof of a unique chemical.
examTips: Name the property that makes the chosen method work.
Use 'suggests' rather than 'proves' when evidence is not unique.
For a table, separate observation from conclusion.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.
